candidate_relations.reason: Vertebrobasilar insufficiency is the vascular interpretation of fluctuating dysarthria and conflicts with myasthenia gravis.
Cardioembolic stroke would produce MRI lesions, which were absent.
Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome is a related NMJ disorder but is a different autoantibody/presynaptic disease.
MELAS causes stroke-like MRI lesions and lactic acidosis, not isolated episodic dysarthria with normal MRI.
ALS is a progressive motor-neuron disease with signs not present (normal strength and reflexes).
Tetanus produces rigidity and spasms, not episodic dysarthria.
Atherosclerotic disease is a mild MRA finding, not the cause of rest-refractory dysarthria.
Multiple sclerosis is a CNS demyelinating disease and MRI was unremarkable.
Neurodegenerative disease does not fit a 20-day fluctuating dysarthria with normal imaging.
A seizure disorder would typically include impaired awareness or postictal findings, which were absent.
Cerebral vasculitis is unsupported by normal MRI, CSF-not-given, and negative rheumatologic panels.
Cerebral vasculopathy is a nonspecific vascular label, not myasthenia gravis.
Botulism is a related NMJ toxin syndrome, typically descending and progressive, not brief daily dysarthric spells.
Transient ischemic attack of the vertebrobasilar system was the initial diagnosis and conflicts with rest-refractory symptoms and myasthenia gravis.
Myasthenia gravis matches the reference diagnosis.
Transient ischemic attack is the same incompatible vascular diagnosis.
Stroke is contradicted by unremarkable MRI/SWI.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: stroke vs MG with normal MRI

candidate_relations.reason: Vertebrobasilar TIA is again the initial incompatible diagnosis.
Basilar migraine would include headache or other aura features that were denied.
Small-vessel disease is a chronic MRI diagnosis; the brain MRI was unremarkable.

case_quality_flags: Episodic dysarthria with normal MRI was first called vertebrobasilar TIA; fatigue and neostigmine tests were negative, so myasthenia is not electrophysiologically confirmed in the card
